w: Moored in Gdynia harbour next to the sailing ship Dar Pomorza, ORP Blyskawica is the only Polish Navy vessel ever awarded the Virtuti Militari, Poland's highest gallantry order, for her World War II service. Built by J. Samuel White in Cowes, this Grom-class destroyer is now the oldest preserved destroyer in the world.
s: The world's oldest preserved WWII destroyer
_facts: Grom-class destroyer, built by J. Samuel White, Cowes, 1935-1937
Only Polish Navy ship awarded the Virtuti Militari
Preserved as a museum ship in Gdynia, oldest preserved destroyer in the world

w: Built in 1909 and later serving as a training ship under German, French and Polish flags, the full-rigged Dar Pomorza now sits preserved as a museum ship in Gdynia harbour, moored beside the destroyer ORP Blyskawica. In 1980 she won the Cutty Sark Trophy, the sailing world's marquee prize for tall ships.
s: A 1909 tall ship that won sailing's top trophy
_facts: Served as training ship in Germany, France and Poland
Won the Cutty Sark Trophy in 1980; preserved as a museum ship in Gdynia

w: Housed in Gdynia's former Maritime Station, the building thousands of Polish emigrants passed through en route abroad between the 1930s and 1979, the Emigration Museum opened in 2015 after a 49.3-million-zloty refurbishment. It tells 200 years of Polish emigration and won the Ziva Award for Best Slavic Museum.
s: Where a century of Polish emigrants departed
_facts: Opened 16 May 2015 in the former Maritime Station (transit building 1930s-1979)
Refurbished at a cost of PLN 49.3 million; won the Ziva Award for Best Slavic Museum in 2018

w: Run by the National Marine Fisheries Research Institute along the South Pier, Gdynia Aquarium has operated under several names since 1971, when it opened as the Oceanographic Museum and Sea Aquarium of the Sea Fisheries Institute. Equal parts public aquarium and research institution, it holds zoological garden status.
s: A public aquarium and sea museum on the South Pier
_facts: Opened 1971 as the Oceanographic Museum and Sea Aquarium of the Sea Fisheries Institute
Operated by the National Marine Fisheries Research Institute
Zoological garden status, located on the South Pier

w: Two wooded summits in Gdynia's Dabrowa district make up Donas hill, its eastern peak carrying a GSM tower with a public viewing terrace 232 metres up, taking in Gdansk, Gdynia, Gdansk Bay and the Hel Peninsula. In March 1945 a battle was fought here between the Red Army and German forces.
s: A hilltop viewing terrace with a WWII battle site
_facts: Twin summits, 206.5m and 205.6m, in Gdynia's Dabrowa district
GSM tower with public viewing terrace at 232m, panoramic views over Gdansk Bay
Site of a March 1945 battle between Red Army and German forces; nearby abandoned cemetery

w: First built during World War I in the resort of Orlowo, this wooden pier grew to 430 metres in the 1920s as Orlowo raced its rival resort Sopot to build the bigger promenade. A 1949 storm wrecked more than half of it, and a 1953 rebuild left it at its current 180 metres, beside the Orlowo Cliff.
s: A storm-battered wooden pier in old Orlowo
_facts: Built during WWI, expanded to 430m in the 1920s amid rivalry with Sopot
Orlowo became a Gdynia borough in June 1935
1949 storm destroyed over half the pier; 1953 renovation left it at 180m today
